n67dc9592c1d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's role in the library movement?
o: He sent his newspaper, books and Bharati free to any group of ten youths opening a village library.
He was one of the Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu.
He sent his newspaper, books and Bharati free to any group of fifty youths opening a village library.
He finished and published the catalogue of printed Telugu books.
n67dc9592c1d.x: The free supply went to any group of ten youths, not fifty, who opened a village library.

nap-history-11-15.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gidugu Rama Murthy – Vyavaharika Bhasha movement
nap-history-11-15.x: Gidugu Rama Murthy fathered the spoken-dialect (Vyavaharika Bhasha) movement; the English-Telugu dictionary was compiled by C.P. Brown.

nap-history-19-10.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about early Telugu libraries in Hyderabad?
o: The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in 1901.
The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in 1898.
It was the first non-government Telugu library in Hyderabad.
The Vignana Chandrika Mandali was founded in 1906.
nap-history-19-10.x: The Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in 1901, not 1898.

na0db77a3a6f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andhra Desa Library Association?
o: It is regarded as the first state-level library association in India.
na0db77a3a6f.x: The Andhra Desa Library Association was founded at Vijayawada, not Madras.

nb8f1f9ef62e.s: The Bengal library association, one of the associations Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya helped found, was established in:
nb8f1f9ef62e.x: The Bengal association came in 1925, after ADLA (1914) and before the Madras association (1928).

new.s: Besides political awakening, the Andhra editors' papers also funded and publicised which movement?
new.x: The same papers that spread political awakening also funded and publicised the library movement.

new.s: The early Telugu paper Andhra Prakasika was edited by:
new.x: Andhra Prakasika was A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu's paper; Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu edited Brahma Prakasika.

new.s: Who was the first editor of Krishna Patrika (1902, Machilipatnam)?
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya co-founded Krishna Patrika and was its first editor; Mutnuri was its famous later editor.

new.s: Who was the first editor of the Telugu daily Andhra Prabha (1938)?
new.x: Khasa Subba Rao was its first editor; Nyapati Narayanamurti edited it later.

new.s: The English weekly Swarajya (1956), started with C. Rajagopalachari's support, was edited by:
new.x: Khasa Subba Rao ran the English Swarajya (1956); Gadicherla's Swarajya was a Telugu paper of 1907.

new.s: Rayyat, the Urdu daily in the list of movement-era papers, was edited by:
new.x: Rayyat was an Urdu daily of M. Narasinga Rao; Suravaram Pratap Reddy edited Golconda Patrika.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (paper – editor) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Andhra Prakasika was edited by A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu; Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu edited Brahma Prakasika.

new.s: Bharati, started by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao in 1924, was a:
new.x: Bharati (1924) was a literary monthly, distinct from his Andhra Patrika (1908).

new.s: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika during:
new.x: Mutnuri edited Krishna Patrika from 1907 until his death in 1945; the paper itself was founded in 1902.

new.s: Who is called the doyen of Telugu journalism?
new.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao, long-time editor of Krishna Patrika, is called the doyen of Telugu journalism.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mutnuri Krishna Rao:
1. He ran the magazine Andhra Bharati for some time.
2. He wrote editorials attacking British government spending.
3. He founded Krishna Patrika in 1902.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are true; Krishna Patrika was founded by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, not Mutnuri.

new.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao funded his public work from which business he founded?
new.x: He founded the Amrutanjan business and used its wealth for public work in a Gandhian trusteeship spirit.

new.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's publishing house, named to popularise the word 'Andhra', was:
new.x: His publishing house was Andhra Granthamala; Vignana Chandrika Granthamala was Komarraju's.

new.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao completed and published the catalogue of printed Telugu books begun by:
new.x: He finished and published the catalogue begun by Velidanda Hanumantha Rao.

new.s: Which of the following titles is NOT associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao?
new.x: Doyen of Telugu journalism is Mutnuri Krishna Rao; the other three are Kasinathuni's titles.

new.s: The Sreebagh Pact was signed at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's Madras house on:
new.x: The Sreebagh Pact was signed at Sreebagh, Madras, on 16 November 1937.

new.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was jailed for sedition in 1908 for which article in Swarajya?
new.x: The article Veerabali in Swarajya led to his sedition conviction in 1908.

new.s: In which year was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao jailed in the Swarajya sedition case?
new.x: He started Swarajya in 1907 and was jailed for sedition in 1908.

new.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was blacklisted from government jobs after the 1907 incident at:
new.x: The 1907 Rajahmundry College incident led to his blacklisting from government service.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (editor – institution) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao – Edward Corporation Library
Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao – Bala Bharati Samithi
new.x: Andhra Granthamala was Kasinathuni's publishing house; Khasa Subba Rao founded the English weeklies Swatantra and Swarajya.

new.s: The Bala Bharati Samithi founded by Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao in 1907 was at:
new.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao founded the Bala Bharati Samithi at Rajahmundry in February 1907.

new.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's Andhra tour of April 1907 is linked with an invitation from:
new.x: Mutnuri invited Bipin Chandra Pal; the G2 2011 key wrongly credited Gadicherla.

new.s: Bipin Chandra Pal delivered his Kakinada lecture on:
new.x: He spoke at Kakinada on 17 April 1907 and gave five lectures at Rajahmundry on 19–24 April 1907.

new.s: 'Air is available freely to all. Knowledge too should be available likewise.' Who said this?
new.x: The words are Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham's, who also presided over the first library conference.

new.s: Sujananda Granthalayam (1894) at Rayakuduru was founded by:
new.x: Kallakuri Narasimha founded it and also the A.O. Hume Reading Room at Kopalle (1895).

new.s: The early Saraswati Granthalayam was located at:
new.x: Saraswati Granthalayam was at Pulivendula; Simhachalapathi Granthalayam was at Vizianagaram.

new.s: Who was the secretary of the Rama Mohana Library, Vijayawada (1911)?
new.x: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya was its secretary; the library later became the central library of Andhra.

new.s: The Andhra Council of Research (1916) was located at:
new.x: The Andhra Council of Research was at Kovvur; the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was at Hyderabad (1901).

new.s: The Gautami Granthalayam at Rajahmundry (1898) was formed by the merger of the Town Hall Library and the:
new.x: Gautami Granthalayam merged the Vasuraya Granthalayam and the Town Hall Library.

new.s: By 1913, about how many libraries existed in Andhra?
new.x: About 125 libraries existed by 1913; 60 libraries sent delegates to the first conference.

new.s: The first Andhra library conference was held at Vijayawada on:
new.x: It met on 10 April 1913, a year before the Andhra Desa Library Association was founded.

new.s: The call for the first library conference was given through Andhra Patrika by Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya and:
new.x: Ayyanki and Suri Venkata Narasimha issued the call through Andhra Patrika.

new.s: Along with Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya, who was a secretary of the Andhra Desa Library Association?
new.x: The secretaries were Ayyanki and Nalam Krishnarao; Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was the first president.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra library movement:
1. The first Andhra library conference was held in 1914.
2. The Andhra Desa Library Association was founded in 1914.
3. Grandhalaya Sarvasvam began in 1915.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The first conference was in 1913, not 1914; ADLA (1914) and Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1915) are correct.

new.s: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam, the periodical of the Andhra Desa Library Association, was a Telugu:
new.x: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1915) was a Telugu quarterly published by ADLA.

new.s: Who edited Andhra Granthalayam, the 1948 revival of Grandhalaya Sarvasvam?
new.x: Andhra Granthalayam, a Telugu-English quarterly revived in January 1948, was edited by P. Rajasekharam.

new.s: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam, the first Telugu journal on library science, is associated with:
new.x: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam was associated with Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya, not Gadicherla.

new.s: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya's library pilgrimage (village tours) ran during:
new.x: The library pilgrimage ran 1934–48, covering 182 villages in West Godavari alone; 1935–42 is Pathuri's boat library.

new.s: Which of the following is linked with mobile library carts for rural book supply?
new.x: Mobile library carts are linked with the Kuppam Bharani library and the Pedasanagallu Sri Rama Prasad Library.

new.s: The All India Public Library Conference of 1919 was held at:
new.x: It was held at Madras in 1919, with Andhra leaders in the lead.

new.s: In which year was the All India Public Library Association set up?
new.x: It was set up in 1919 by decision of the All India Public Library Conference at Madras.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (year – library law)?
new.x: The Madras Public Libraries Act was passed in 1948, not 1957.

new.s: Zilla Grandhalaya Samsthas were created under the:
new.x: The AP Public Libraries Act, 1960 created Zilla Grandhalaya Samsthas; the 1948 Madras Act funded libraries by a cess.

new.s: The first session of the Andhra Mahasabha was held at:
new.x: Library-based awakening led to the Andhra Jana Sangham and the Andhra Mahasabha, whose first session was at Jogipet.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the early Telugu libraries of Hyderabad State?
new.x: Gautami Granthalayam was at Rajahmundry; the other three belonged to Hyderabad State.

new.s: Among the Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu, who is described as the 'radical mobiliser'?
new.x: Gadicherla mobilised people, Ayyanki built institutions and Kasinathuni gave money and political backing.

new.s: In the Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's role was:
new.x: Kasinathuni financed and politically backed the movement; Ayyanki built institutions.

new.s: Who is called 'Andhra Desa Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi' (Architect of the Andhra Library Movement)?
new.x: The Roopasilpi title belongs to Pathuri Nagabhushanam; Pitamaha is Ayyanki.

new.s: Pathuri Nagabhushanam received the Kala Prapoorna from Andhra University in:
new.x: Andhra University conferred the Kala Prapoorna on him in 1975.

new.s: Who is known as 'Andhra Charitra Pitamaha'?
new.x: Andhra Charitra Pitamaha is Komarraju; Granthalaya Pitamaha is Ayyanki.

new.s: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya was elected General Secretary of the All India Public Library Association at its second conference in:
new.x: He organised the Madras conference of November 1919 and was elected General Secretary at the second conference, December 1923.

new.s: The Indian Library Association, formed at Calcutta, dates from:
new.x: The Indian Library Association came in 1933; the All India Public Library Association dates from 1919.

new.s: Which journal did Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya edit?
new.x: Ayyanki edited Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1915); the other three were Gadicherla's papers.

new.s: Gadicherla renamed the Ceded Districts 'Rayalaseema' at the 1928 Andhra Mahasabha held at:
new.x: The name Rayalaseema was given at the 1928 Nandyal Andhra Mahasabha.

new.s: In which year was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao president of the library association?
new.x: He was president in 1946; Sarvottama Bhavan opened in 1949 and Rayalaseema was named in 1928.

new.s: The Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu, started by Pathuri Nagabhushanam as a schoolboy, later served about how many villages?
new.x: It later served 40 villages; 160 villages were covered through the Guntur Library Association.

new.s: As Secretary of the Guntur Library Association, Pathuri Nagabhushanam set up libraries in about:
new.x: He set up libraries in about 160 villages and new buildings for 28.

new.s: Who drafted and moved the Madras Public Libraries Bill, 1938 in the Madras Assembly?
new.x: Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya moved the 1938 Bill, not Ayyanki.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (initiative – leader) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: AP Public Libraries Act, 1960 drafting – Pathuri
new.x: The 1938 Madras Public Libraries Bill was drafted and moved by Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya.

new.s: Velaga Venkatappayya led library tours in which taluks?
new.x: Velaga Venkatappayya, the 'Library Gandhi', toured Bhimavaram, Tadepalligudem, Kovvur and Guntur taluks.

new.s: Whose gift bought the building named Sarvottama Bhavan?
new.x: Komma Sitaramayya's gift bought the building through the Andhra Granthalaya Dharma Samstha (1946).

new.s: Along with Gadicherla, who was a co-founder of the Vignana Chandrika Mandali (1906)?
new.x: Komarraju founded it with co-founders including Gadicherla and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.

new.s: Sarvottama Bhavan, named in Gadicherla's honour, was opened in:
new.x: It opened in 1949; the building was acquired through the Andhra Granthalaya Dharma Samstha in 1946.

new.s: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya's 136th birth anniversary in July 2026 was marked at the:
new.x: It was marked on 25 July 2026 at the Tagore Library, Bandar Road, Vijayawada.
